atlas-gr.0117: Silence is common: To Vima’s February 2026 report quotes graduates who sent more than 50 and more than 100 CVs with only automatic replies, and one whose employer disappeared after saying she was hired. We did not establish typical time to offer or dress norms.
atlas-gr.0118: The most common contract is full-time and indefinite; the employer must give the material terms in writing no later than two months after you start. Contractual hours are 40 a week, with statutory limits of 45 hours for a five-day week.
atlas-gr.0119: Private employers pay a 13th monthly salary at Christmas plus Easter and summer-leave allowances; the minimum monthly salary was €920 from 1 April 2026.
atlas-gr.0120: An employer guide says probation is at most six months for indefinite contracts and that in the first 12 months a contract can be ended without notice or severance. We did not establish whether graduates negotiate or how long employers give to decide.
atlas-gr.0121: For a non-EU hire the employer files an electronic request with the regional migration authority for the quota-bound Metaklisi procedure: a contract of at least six months, housing guarantee and pay at least the legal minimum, then a national visa and an E.4 permit. The quota is set by a biennial joint ministerial decision by region and profession.
atlas-gr.0122: An EU Blue Card hire is decided within 90 days, or 30 days if the employer is registered as an accredited sponsor. Few graduate programmes are open to non-Greek speakers: the two read require Greek and English at C2 or excellent Greek and English.
atlas-gr.0123: Ask early and say whether you speak Greek. This is our reading; no page states what employers want to hear.
atlas-gr.0124: Portals and public services: kariera.gr; DYPA (dypa.gov.gr) and its EURES advisers; ASEP (asep.gr) for public competitions; EURES for jobs across the EU.
atlas-gr.0125: Employer pages: HELLENiQ ENERGY’s Empowering Future Leaders, METLEN’s Engineers in Action, Deloitte Greece’s student internships, Pfizer’s Center for Digital Innovation in Thessaloniki.
atlas-gr.0126: Fairs and university offices: Career.Days Athens each September and university career offices such as that of the University of Macedonia in Thessaloniki.
atlas-gr.0127: Applying to the big programmes without Greek: HELLENiQ ENERGY asks for Greek and English at C2 and METLEN for excellent Greek and English.
atlas-gr.0128: Missing the autumn window: METLEN’s applications close on 20 October, and DYPA’s graduate posts were open for only three weeks in July and August.
atlas-gr.0129: Ignoring the men’s requirement: both programmes ask for completed military service or a legal exemption.
atlas-gr.0130: Sending a long CV or letter: EURES says one to two pages for the CV and no more than one typed page for the letter.
atlas-gr.0131: Taking entry-level ads at face value: To Vima reports that ads for junior roles routinely demand two or three years of experience, so apply anyway and use connections.
atlas-gr.0132: HELLENiQ ENERGY requires excellent Greek and English at C2 level and runs its application platform in Greek only; METLEN asks for excellent Greek and English for its Greek positions.
atlas-gr.0133: A PwC Greece accounting-outsourcing graduate posting for Thessaloniki, advertised through a university career office (deadline 11 July 2025), asks for proficient spoken and written Greek and English.
atlas-gr.0134: Pfizer’s Thessaloniki hub works on more than 200 global digital projects, and Accenture’s junior .NET listing states no language requirement; neither page says Greek is needed. English is our reading, not a stated requirement.
atlas-gr.0135: The ASEP portal for public competitions and the DYPA registry are in Greek; no English version of the ASEP site was found.
atlas-gr.0136: Eurostat’s figures show 64.0% of Greek tertiary graduates aged 20 to 34 who left education up to three years earlier in work in 2025, the lowest of the 36 countries listed (EU 85.3%), against 80.3% for all graduates of that age. We found no return-offer or conversion rate for Greece.
atlas-gr.0137: After the crisis, graduate unemployment more than doubled, from 7% in 2009 to 17.1% in 2017, and many graduates left; in a 2025 survey 38% of workers under 30 said their job was unrelated to their studies.
atlas-gr.0138: To Vima reports (24 February 2026) that youth unemployment fell from 29.7% in 2021 to 13% in 2025 but that entry-level ads routinely demand two or three years of experience, and many graduates end up in seasonal work.
atlas-gr.0139: EU, EEA and Swiss citizens may work from the first day; the employer registers the job in the ERGANI II system before you start.
atlas-gr.0140: Staying over three months, register in person at the police aliens department; the certificate never expires and costs €0.50.
atlas-gr.0141: You need a tax number (AFM) and a social-security number (AMKA) to rent, work and see a doctor.
atlas-gr.0143: Full-time admission to an accredited Greek university, then the D visa, and the permit online at services.migration.gov.gr, issued for the whole course.
atlas-gr.0144: You may work part time up to 20 hours a week (80 a month) with no separate authorisation.
atlas-gr.0145: A non-EU student with a permit from another EU country can study here up to 360 days with no Greek visa, after notifying the migration ministry.
atlas-gr.0148: Travel insurance is refused: the policy must state three set covers, starting with €1,500 for doctors and medicines.
atlas-gr.0149: For students of foreign universities: a three-way traineeship agreement with a Greek host, which also undertakes to cover living and return costs, for up to six months. An internship within a Greek degree is covered by the student permit.
atlas-gr.0151: Permit to look for work or start a business (H.11)
atlas-gr.0152: After a Greek bachelor’s, master’s or PhD, or a research project: 12 months, not extendable, applied for online before the student permit expires. A qualified job then converts it inside Greece, outside the quotas.
atlas-gr.0154: A contract of at least six months in a highly qualified job and a three-year degree, or five years of experience (three in the last seven for IT); the card lasts three years, decisions take 30 days with an accredited employer, and family joins at once with the right to work.
atlas-gr.0156: Salary, shortage jobs and recent graduates
atlas-gr.0160: Hiring from abroad for ordinary jobs runs on two-year quotas by region and occupation: the employer requests clearance online, then you get the D visa, at no less than the minimum wage.
atlas-gr.0163: A hosting agreement with an accredited Greek research body or university, which covers return costs; family reunion at once.
atlas-gr.0164: Academic scholarships from public bodies are free of income tax.
atlas-gr.0167: Greece has working-holiday agreements only with Australia and Canada.
atlas-gr.0168: Australians aged 18 to 30 (500 places a year) and Canadians aged 18 to 35 can stay up to 12 months; apply only at a Greek consulate in those countries.
atlas-gr.0169: Up to 90 days in any 180 with no local work; other nationalities may need a Schengen visa.
atlas-gr.0171: Workers who move their tax residence to Greece pay half the income tax on their employment income for seven tax years.
atlas-gr.0172: Nothing to arrange in advance: you may enter with a passport or ID card and work from day one, once your employer has registered the job in the ERGANI II system.
atlas-gr.0173: Get documents apostilled in the issuing country first, then translated in Greece by a translator registered at metafraseis.services.gov.gr: Greek offices refuse translations made before the apostille. A foreign criminal record counts for only 3 months.
atlas-gr.0174: Apply for the national D visa at a Greek consulate: €180, or €90 for study.
atlas-gr.0175: Paper leases count for nothing: your landlord registers the lease on Taxisnet and you accept it online with your tax number (AFM). If you stay with someone, they file a sworn declaration on gov.gr.
atlas-gr.0176: After 3 months, register in person at a police Aliens Department, with your enrolment and European Health Insurance Card if you study. The paper certificate costs €0.50, is issued the same day and does not expire; in Athens there are no bookings, so queue from about 4:30 in the morning.
atlas-gr.0177: Before your D visa expires, apply online at services.migration.gov.gr for the residence permit (€150, plus €16 for the card); the receipt with a QR code lets you work until the biometrics appointment. Filing late makes you irregular, with fines of €600 to €1,200.
atlas-gr.0178: Get a tax number (AFM) first: without it you cannot register a lease or sign a work contract. Apply at the tax office, naming a resident tax representative, or through myAADElive.
atlas-gr.0179: Then ask for a social security number (AMKA) at a citizens’ service centre (KEP) or e-EFKA; the PAAYPA number is only for asylum seekers.
atlas-gr.0180: EU students register with their European Health Insurance Card.
atlas-gr.0181: Generic travel policies are refused for the permit: the insurance must state €1,500 for doctor visits and medicines, €10,000 for hospital stays (with at most 20% excess) and €15,000 for permanent disability.
